ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), Act No. 10062, as amended; Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Financial Services Commission Regulations on Identification and Reporting of Financial Transactions and Beneficial Owners; Korean Commercial Act, Articles 289, 292-2, 292-3 and 317; Korean Real Name Financial Transactions Act; Value-Added Tax Act, Article 5(1). Korea does not maintain a public UBO register; beneficial ownership data is collected by financial institutions and disclosed only to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, the National Tax Service, the Financial Services Commission and authorized court/tax authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Companies Registry or Registrar of Companies in the country of the ultimate parent's incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Foreign Companies Registry -> Competent Authority in the country of origin affixes a Hague Apostille -> Korean certified translation -> submission to Korean registry, courts, banks or AML reviewers. Consular Legalization Path (non-member states only): Foreign Companies Registry -> Foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> Legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction -> Korean certified translation -> submission. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never combine apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Same national Companies Registry or Registrar of Companies that issued the parent's Certificate of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Issuance by Companies Registry -> Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin -> Korean certified translation -> submission. Consular Legalization Path: Issuance by Companies Registry -> Country-of-origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization -> Korean certified translation -> submission. Do not add a second authentication method to an already apostilled document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the local Incorporator and Inaugural Directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the ultimate parent company, certifying secretary or corporate governance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Board Resolution executed -> Notary public in the country of origin -> Apostille by the country's competent Hague Authority -> Korean certified translation -> use. Consular Legalization Path: Board Resolution executed -> Country-of-origin notary -> Country-of-origin MFA -> Korean Consulate legalization -> Korean certified translation -> use. The two paths are exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the Ultimate Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate parent company's corporate secretary or registered agent certified as true copy from the parent's statutory records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Certified copy by parent corporate secretary -> Notary public -> Apostille by competent authority of the originating state -> Korean certified translation -> submission. Consular Legalization Path: Certified copy -> Notary public -> Country-of-origin MFA -> Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization -> Korean certified translation -> submission. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; never use both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Ultimate Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or corporate banking branch of the ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter is issued on bank letterhead and the bank officer's signature is notarized; if the Korean recipient bank requires foreign public-document status, the Hague Apostille path may be applied in contracting states, while non-contracting states follow consular legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are not sequential and never both apply to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Passport Copy and UBO Declaration Statement for Each Individual Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public in the UBO's country of residence or nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path for states party to the Apostille Convention: Notarized passport copy/UBO statement -> Competent Authority affixes apostille -> Korean certified translation -> Korean AML/KYC file. Non-member states: Notarized document -> Foreign MFA -> Korean Consulate legalization -> Korean certified translation. The two paths are alternatives; a document apostilled must not later be sent for consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any shareholder, director, statutory auditor, authorized signatory, lessee, escrow counterparty, or ultimate beneficial owner, the Korean entity must conduct real-time screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, FATF Public Statements, and the sanctions and prohibition designations maintained by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The protocol must verify the 25 percent beneficial ownership threshold, screen family members and close associates of foreign PEPs and domestic prominent public functionaries, run negative news/adverse media checks, categorise counterparties from high-risk jurisdictions as enhanced due diligence, and monitor all SWIFT wires, aircraft lease rental payments, and escrow inflows on an ongoing basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) at ris.registration.go.kr and the Commercial Registration System of the National Court Administration at the District Court Registry Office with jurisdiction over the registered head office address.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must be entered in the Korean alphabet (Hangul). An English trade name may be used in parallel commercial documents, but the legal registered name must contain the Korean-form expression of a Chusik Hoesa. The four-tier naming doctrine is: (1) distinctive brand mark; (2) descriptive commercial purpose in Hangul, such as aircraft engine leasing; (3) the legal-form designation 'Chusik Hoesa' or the equivalent Korean suffix; and (4) an English transliteration of the brand for aviation contracts and SWIFT/escrow communications. Foreign words are transliterated according to the National Institute of Korean Language standards rather than translated only, and names confusingly similar to earlier registered companies are rejected under the Korean Commercial Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the IROS or Registry Office returns the name clearance, the incorporator must submit a written objection to the head of the competent District Court Registry Office within 14 days under Korean Commercial Act Articles 292-2 and 292-3. The objection must identify the rejected name, the rejection notice number, the intended aircraft engine leasing business scope, and evidence of brand use or requested alternative transliteration. The registry will review and issue a reconsideration decision. If still refused, the applicant may apply for review by the Supreme Court Registration Review Committee and thereafter pursue administrative litigation, while Korean counsel simultaneously files a newly cleared alternative name to prevent delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is rejected by the National Tax Service and most Korean banks for VAT and corporate tax registration, and is unsuitable for a medium-risk aviation asset licensing business. The Korean Commercial Act and VAT Act require an actual head office in Korea where the books, accounting records, board minutes, invoices, lease files and management personnel are physically accessible. A serviced office or flex-space with a real lease, dedicated desk or suite, signage, and on-site staff may be acceptable, but a P.O. Box or forwarding-only agent is not permissible for aircraft engine dry-leasing operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) lease agreement in the name of the Chusik Hoesa; (2) visible corporate nameplate at the registered address; (3) utility bills and internet/phone invoices; (4) physical accounting books and VAT filing records; (5) presence of the statutory local director or staff; (6) signed board minutes for major lease transactions; and (7) bank/escrow correspondences. Quantified risk of an unannounced physical visit by National Tax Service or municipal tax inspectors is 10-15 percent in the first two years for a compliant physical office, rising to 30-45 percent for a virtual-office only structure, and above 60 percent if high-value aircraft lease invoices or frequent capital disposals trigger a tax audit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 289 (contents of the Articles of Incorporation), 292 (subscription of shares), 295 (payment of subscription price), 301 (effective date of incorporation), 312-317 (registration of incorporation), 389 (Representative Director), 393 (resolution of the Board of Directors), and 434 (special resolution of shareholders, where relevant).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered office, operating through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) at i.registry.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration, Notarized Articles of Incorporation, Certificate of Stock Subscription Payment, and the certificate of deposit issued by a licensed Korean bank holding the provisional stock subscription account.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - under the Commercial Act of Korea there is no legal minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa; the company may fix a nominal par value in the Articles of Incorporation, provided at least one share is issued and the full subscription price is paid-in at incorporation. For bank creditworthiness and aircraft-lessor market acceptance, a paid-up capital of at least KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 75,000) is commercially recommended but not legally mandated. No blocked escrow account is required by general Korean corporate law; subscription funds must be deposited into a provisional stock subscription account opened in the company's name, and the account cannot be withdrawn until the incorporation registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA) IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA

WHEREAS the incorporation proceedings of the Company are being implemented under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and the initial subscribed capital has been allotted to the founding shareholders, and a notarial certificate of incorporation has been prepared; and all actions necessary to complete registration with the competent Registry Court require Board oversight,

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors, having satisfied itself that a quorum is lawfully present, resolves as follows:

1. Share Capital. The subscription of [___] ordinary shares of par value [___] Korean Won each, for an aggregate paid-in capital of [___] Korean Won, is ratified and confirmed. The Board acknowledges that the full subscription price has been deposited or remitted to the provisional subscription account duly opened by the incorporators and held in trust for the Company until the completion of incorporation; such account shall not be drawn upon except by the Representative Director after the commercial registry certificate has been issued.

2. Registered Office. The registered office and administrative headquarters of the Company are fixed at [address] in the Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is directed to prepare a lease contract and any consent of the landlord required for the registration.

3. Banking Authority. The Company shall open the following accounts with [Bank] - a Korean Won corporate operating account, a USD foreign currency account, and any other accounts necessary for deposit of future rental payments and escrow funds received under aircraft engine dry leases. The Representative Director is authorized to execute all account documents, to submit the Company's corporate resolution and constitutional documents to the bank's compliance team, and to act with one additional joint signatory as follows: for amounts exceeding USD 50,000, any payment instruction must be co-signed by the Finance Director.

4. Statutory Officers. The following officers are appointed effective immediately: [Name] as Representative Director, [Name] as Chief Finance Officer, [Name] as standing Auditor. Each appointee has accepted their role and undertakes to act within the authority set forth in the Articles of Incorporation and the Commercial Act.

5. Completion. The Representative Director is authorized to file the incorporation registration application with the District Court, to apply for the Business Registration Certificate from the competent National Tax Service office, and to execute any ancillary documents required for the Company's lawful formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Subscription Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public registered with the Korean Bar Association in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must draft and sign the Articles of Incorporation in Korean and English, clearly setting out the exact corporate name ending with 'Chusik Hoesa', the corporate object of turbofan aircraft engine dry leasing, registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, and the names and seals of the founding officers. All articles shall be executed before a notary public, who will prepare a notarial certificate verifying that the founders appeared and signed. If a non-resident founder cannot appear, a power of attorney must be notarized in the home country and apostilled or consular-legalized. The notary must approve the Korean corporate name and ensure no conflict with existing registered trade names. After the notarization, the original Articles are kept by the company and a duplicate is submitted to the Court Registry. If the notary refuses due to defective corporate purposes or capital clauses, the founders must amend the Articles and re-notarize before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean and English
Founder identification documents or passports
Power of attorney if a local agent or proxy is used
Proof of land ownership or lease contract for registered office
Notary fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary questions the lawful purpose, the Board shall revise the Articles to expressly include ISIC 5223 activity titles, resubmit within one business day, and obtain a corrected notarial certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Stock Subscription Price into a Provisional Subscription Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, with AML/KYC compliance division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization of the Articles, the incorporators open a provisional stock subscription deposit account at a bank legally operating in Korea. The bank account must be opened in the name of the Company-to-be, with a designation such as 'Chusik Hoesa (Incorporation in Progress)'. Each founder must pay in full the nominal amount of their subscribed shares by remittance or direct deposit; the bank will issue a deposit receipt itemizing each subscriber and the paid amount. The subscription price must not be withdrawn until the Company is registered. The deposit certificate is required by the court as evidence of capital payment. If the bank's AML risk assessment requires explanation of the source of the funds, the founders must provide a signed source-of-funds declaration and certified bank statements. This stage is completed when the certificate contains the company's name and all subscriber names and amounts.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of subscription
Founder passport copies
Business plan and source of funds declaration
Account opening application with bank AML forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, submit the requested beneficial ownership data and re-submit the provisional account application within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the District Court / IRO Electronic Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court of the registered office; filing accomplished via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal representative or an attorney submits the incorporation registration application to the Registration Division of the District Court of the place of the registered office. Alternatively, the company may file electronically via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) by uploading the application and scanned attachments. The court clerk will examine whether the Articles, capital deposit certificate, and the minutes of the directors' meeting comply with Articles 289, 295, 301 and 317 of the Commercial Act. The application must include a written declaration that the incorporators have complied with the capital payment obligation and that the registered office exists. Upon approval, the court enters the company into the commercial registry and a certified copy of the commercial register (Jung-deung) is issued. The incorporation date is the date of the court's registration. If the court requests correction, all defects must be cured and resubmitted within five business days.
required_dossiers: Application for Incorporation Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Stock Subscription Payment from the bank
Deposit certificate of the provisional subscription account
Acceptance letters of directors and auditor (or indication of appointment)
Lease contract or evidence of entitlement to the registered office
Passport copies of officers and founders
Power of attorney if an attorney files the registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order (Bojjongtongji), file the corrected documents within the prescribed five business-day period; if rejected, engage a Korean licensed attorney to verify the Commercial Act compliance and re-file immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with National Tax Service and Activation of Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (district tax office of the registered office) via Home Tax; bank branch of the provisional subscription account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must apply to the National Tax Service for a Business Registration Certificate within 20 days of incorporation. The application is filed with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office, using the Home Tax electronic system. The NTS will issue a Business Registration Certificate with a registration number for VAT and corporate income tax. Concurrently, the company activates the provisional stock subscription account at the bank into a regular corporate account by presenting the commercial registry certificate, the Business Registration Certificate, the personal IDs and passport copies of the directors, the board resolution naming the account signatories, and the company's corporate seal. The bank will complete verification under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the account can then receive USD escrow transfers and sell aircraft engine leases. If import or export of physical engines is anticipated, the company must also register with Korea Customs Service as an importer/exporter and obtain a foreign exchange transaction unit (Tower).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of commercial registry certificate (Jung-deung)
Articles of Incorporation
Business Registration Certificate application form
Corporate seal registration certificate
Lease contract of registered office
Passports and internal IDs of all directors
Board resolution authorizing bank account signatories
Bank account activation form and tax invoice reporting information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS questions the VAT registration, submit an explanation of the foreign lease income under the VAT Act and request expedited review; if the bank delays account activation, escalate to the branch compliance officer with the commercial registry certificate and board resolution in hand.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) - Aviation Policy Bureau for any aviation asset registration; National Tax Service for standard business licensing; Korea Customs Service for cross-border engine import or export; Financial Services Commission if foreign exchange escrow is treated as a foreign exchange business.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None applicable - pure dry leasing of aircraft engines does not constitute a licensed air transport business under the Aviation Safety Act, nor a manufacturing or warehousing operation. A standard Business Registration Certificate (Saupja-deungrok) under the Value-Added Tax Act is mandatory for Korean corporate operation. If the engine is physically brought to Korea for storage or onward leasing, a customs import declaration under the Customs Act and an MOLIT engine registration technical inspection may be required; if the company operates no physical facility, no industry-specific operating license is imposed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MoE) through the Korea Environmental Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full Environmental Impact Assessment or Environmental Registration is required because the dry-leasing enterprise does not create any physical industrial installation, emission source, or hazardous facility. For any incidental storage of engines in a leased airport hangar, the airport operator's own Environmental Impact Assessment for the aerodrome covers the category; no separate EIA application by the lessor is triggered under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the leasing entity has zero routine discharge of wastewater, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), or hazardous waste attributable to its administrative office. Any incidental hydraulic fluid, oil residue, or cleaning-agent emissions arising during engine maintenance or MRO shall be managed exclusively by the MRO service provider, which must hold emission permits consistent with the Clean Air Conservation Act and Wastes Control Act (e.g., VOC concentration limits for coating and degreasing operations, hazard waste manifest filings).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate: required for the registered office only if the floor area exceeds 150 square meters under the Fire Prevention, Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control Act; otherwise a simple fire-safety inspection declaration suffices for commercial office premises. If the lessor stores engines at an airport, the hangar/ground operator maintains the Civil Defense fire clearance and fire suppression facility permits, and the lessor must ensure the lease contract contains an indemnity regarding engine storage in a fire-safe zone. Occupational Safety: administrative office workplaces must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by appointing a safety supervisor if 10 or more full-time workers are employed; material handling of aircraft engines is outside the lessor's internal operations, as the physical possession and maintenance is carried out by third-party MRO providers with their own KOSHA approvals and structural load inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, accessible through the HomeTax online portal at www.hometax.go.kr; export and customs validation is coordinated with the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Korea must apply for a Business Registration Certificate (Saeupja Deungjeongjeung) through HomeTax or the local district tax office before commencing taxable activity. Where the foreign entity has no domestic place of business, a statutory tax representative must be appointed. The tax representative submits the foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution or power of attorney, domestic business address evidence, and lease or contract documentation. The NTS assigns a unique 10-digit business registration number, which functions as the VAT identification number for subsequent tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or analogous entity classification election exists under Korean tax law. A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a standalone domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act. Korean-resident corporate groups may elect consolidated corporate tax return treatment under Article 76-9 of the Corporate Tax Act, but foreign corporations with only a Korean branch are not eligible. VAT grouping is not permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No KRW monetary threshold. VAT registration is mandatory for every entrepreneur, including a foreign non-resident supplier with a Korean taxable nexus, making taxable supplies in Korea regardless of annual turnover. Foreign suppliers without a domestic place of business must appoint a tax representative and register through HomeTax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices between registered businesses must be issued as electronic tax invoices and transmitted to the NTS through HomeTax in near real-time. Transmission may be effected through the HomeTax user interface, EDI, or machine-to-machine API integration. Export customs declarations must be filed electronically through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system. Digital stamping is not used, but real-time national tax clearance of e-tax invoices and daily reporting of cash receipts through approved VAN service providers are mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 21(1) of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act for exported goods and under Article 21(2) for services supplied to overseas users. For an aircraft engine dry leasing transaction, the taxpayer must demonstrate that the engine was physically exported or delivered to a non-resident lessee, title and possession or control passed to the foreign lessee, the engine is used wholly outside Korean customs territory, and the consideration is received in foreign currency from offshore. The taxpayer must retain the executed lease agreement, engine serial number documentation, customs export declaration, transport or delivery receipts, and foreign exchange remittance evidence.

stage_3.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are subject to documentary review and risk-based audit by the National Tax Service and the Korea Customs Service. If export or offshore service conditions are not satisfied, the unpaid VAT is clawed back with interest, and penalty surcharges apply under the Framework Act on National Taxes: up to 40% of the understated output tax for fraudulent misreporting and up to 10% for negligent under-reporting. Fraudulent issuance or use of false export evidence may trigger criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and extension of the retroactive assessment period to 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including cross-border lease payments, subject to reporting requirements under FETA. Capital account transactions, such as inbound equity injections and foreign loans, require prior declaration or approval from the MOEF or delegated banks. Profit remittance (dividends) is permitted under current account rules, but requires tax clearance and submission of audited financial statements. No significant hurdles exist for genuine commercial transactions, but strict documentation and reporting are mandatory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 17 of FETA and related regulations, export proceeds (including lease income from foreign lessees) must be repatriated to Korea within 6 months from the date of export (or service provision). There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; however, the proceeds must be received in a designated foreign currency account or converted to KRW and reported to the designated foreign exchange bank. Failure to repatriate within the timeline triggers penalties and potential criminal liability.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. South Korea does not recognize offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licenses for domestic corporate banking. Foreign fintech entities (e.g., Revolut, Wise) cannot provide local KRW accounts or act as primary clearing agents. They may be used as ancillary payment channels, but all statutory FX reporting and tax compliance must be executed through a licensed Korean bank. Legal constraints under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and FETA prohibit unlicensed cross-border deposit-taking and payment services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the company's authorized signatories (directors or officers) is generally required for initial account opening at Korean banks. Remote opening is permitted only for existing customers or under exceptional circumstances with apostilled corporate documents, notarized board resolutions, and a video interview. For a newly established Chusik Hoesa with foreign ownership, at least one director must appear in person at the bank branch to complete the KYC interview and sign the account mandate. Alternatively, a local attorney-in-fact with a notarized power of attorney may appear, but the bank may still require a video call with the ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., lessee or engine manufacturer located in a FATF grey-listed country)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full corporate registry extracts of the counterparty, audited financial statements, lease agreement with clear commercial rationale, and a risk assessment report. Include a detailed explanation of the transaction chain, beneficial ownership structure, and any third-party intermediaries. Obtain a legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming the legitimacy of the transaction and compliance with UN sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction pattern (e.g., large lump-sum lease prepayment or frequent changes to payment routing)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the original lease agreement, engine maintenance logs, insurance certificates, and a board resolution approving the transaction. Provide a cash flow forecast and explanation of the commercial necessity. Maintain a complete audit trail of all communications with the lessee and any brokers. Be prepared to provide the bank with a sworn affidavit from the CFO detailing the economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (Politically Exposed Person) involvement in the ownership or management
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a comprehensive CV and background check of the PEP, a declaration of the source of funds, and a legal opinion on the legitimacy of the investment. Submit the company's internal AML policy and evidence of enhanced due diligence performed. Obtain a reference letter from a reputable financial institution in the PEP's home country.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For initial equity injection from foreign shareholders, the funds must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to the company's capital escrow account at a Korean bank. The remittance must include a clear purpose code (e.g., 'Equity Investment' under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act) and the company's business registration number. The bank will verify the transaction against the foreign investment declaration filed with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA). For loans from foreign shareholders, a loan agreement must be registered with the MOEF, and the funds must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank. All inbound remittances must be reported to the Bank of Korea within 30 days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to foreign engine manufacturers or maintenance providers, the company may use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers or commercial letters of credit (L/C) for larger procurement contracts. The bank will require the underlying invoice, purchase order, and customs documentation (if applicable). For lease payments received from foreign lessees, the company must ensure the funds are credited to a foreign currency account and then either converted to KRW or retained, subject to the 6-month repatriation rule. For outbound payments, the company must submit a 'Foreign Exchange Transaction Application' to the bank, and the bank will verify the transaction against the FETA reporting thresholds. For payments exceeding USD 50,000, additional supporting documents are required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency forwards (deliverable) with Korean banks for KRW/USD and KRW/EUR, subject to underlying exposure verification.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without onshore deliverability, but only through licensed Korean banks with MOF approval.
Currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for long-term lease receivables, requiring a documented underlying exposure and prior approval from the Bank of Korea.
FX options (plain vanilla) for hedging lease payment volatility, permitted with a licensed bank and subject to position limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Income Tax Return (법인세 과세표준 및 세액 신고서) including annual financial statements and International Related-Party Transaction Schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (by March 31 for a calendar-year company); automatic 1-month extension to April 30 for corporations subject to external audit; further approval-based extension available for certain foreign-source income entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled-return surcharge of 20% of the deficient tax; underreporting surcharge of 10%; daily late-payment interest on unpaid tax (currently 0.025% per day); the NTS may cancel the business registration for a company with no filing for 12 consecutive months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surcharge Return (주민세 법인세분 신고서)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory deadline as the national corporate income tax return (by March 31; extended to April 30 for externally audited companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same surcharge regime as national corporate income tax (20% unfiled-return and 10% underreporting surcharges); daily late-payment interest assessed by the local government on unpaid local surcharge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by February 15 of the year following the reporting year (calendar-year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; suspension or revocation of foreign investment incentives and registration benefits; repeat non-filing may lead to cancellation of foreign-invested enterprise status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report (감사보고서) delivery and filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (with the corporate income tax return); Financial Supervisory Service (via DART) for certain registered companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by June 30 for a calendar-year company); audited financial statements must accompany the corporate tax return filed by March 31 or April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to KRW 100,000,000 under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; FSS may designate an auditor; unaudited financial statements constitute an incomplete tax filing and attract unfiled-return surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Resolutions Registration (주주총회 결의등기)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting must be held within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by June 30 for a calendar-year company); resolutions appointing or re-appointing directors and approving financial statements must be registered within 15 days of the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine (과태료) under the Korean Commercial Act for delayed or omitted registration; Korea does not provide for automatic administrative strike-off, but a court may dissolve a company that has been inactive for a prolonged period under Commercial Act Article 520-2.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (외부감사법) and its Presidential Decree, a Chusik Hoesa must appoint an independent statutory auditor if, at the end of the preceding fiscal year, its total assets reach at least KRW 50 billion; certain foreign-invested enterprises, financial companies, and companies meeting revenue or employee criteria may be subject to lower compulsory audit thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) mandatory for all externally audited companies; private Chusik Hoesa not subject to mandatory audit may prepare financial statements under Korean GAAP (일반기업회계기준) for corporate tax filing purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean private Chusik Hoesa is not subject to a general annual UBO confirmation filing; ownership data is refreshed through the Register of Members upon each share transfer, and foreign-invested enterprises report shareholder and ownership changes through the annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Report due by February 15. Beneficial ownership transparency obligations apply only to financial-sector entities, real-estate title registration, and FATCA/CRS procedures, not to ordinary annual commercial maintenance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (주주명부) maintained at the registered head office
Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors (이사·감사 명부)
Minute Book (의사록) containing minutes of shareholders' meetings and board of directors' meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% for the bracket exceeding KRW 3,000,000,000 (national Corporate Income Tax); 26.4% combined after the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket statutory tax holiday for aircraft-engine dry lessors. Targeted incentives include: (i) Facility Investment Tax Credit of 2–3% for productive assets, including flight equipment; (ii) R&D tax credits of up to 30% for qualifying aviation-engineering research; (iii) employment and new-growth-engine industry tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; (iv) for foreign-invested corporations with high-technology advanced business facilities, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act permits MOF-approved reductions of corporate income tax, generally up to 100% for the first five years and 50% for the following two years, or an expedited deduction of investment assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax final return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act; electronically filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr). Mandatory e-filing applies to corporations whose total assets exceed KRW 10,000,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus a semi-annual interim prepayment return for the first half of the fiscal year; large corporations with gross revenue exceeding KRW 50,000,000,000 are additionally subject to monthly prepayment/estimated accrual rules for corporate income tax purposes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year. A December 31 fiscal-year-end therefore requires filing by March 31 of the following year; one non-renewable one-month extension may be granted by the NTS upon documented request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chusik Hoesa registered name, business registration number, representative director, corporate tax classification, business type (ISIC 5223 / NAICS 532411), fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign shareholders are present, enter each non-resident shareholder's full legal name, nationality, jurisdiction of tax residence, and foreign tax identification number; attach certificate of incorporation and evidence of direct shareholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Statement of Financial Position and Equity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance-sheet inputs covering aircraft-engine assets, accumulated depreciation, lease receivables, security deposits, related-party payables, and shareholder equity including subscribed capital and retained earnings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all non-resident equity injections and loan accounts; for an aircraft-engine dry-leasing entity, clearly distinguish operational lease deposits from financing liabilities; attach foreign-exchange bank receipts for each capital contribution by a non-resident shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross rental revenue from the operational dry lease of turbofan engines, including basic lease rents, utilisation-based supplements, end-of-lease adjustment payments, and contractual maintenance reserve receipts that have the character of income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Korean-source or treaty-sourced income relevant to the Korean entity; on the accompanying schedules, isolate cross-border lease payments from foreign affiliates so that the NTS can apply Article 11 of the International Tax Adjustment Act to the related-party transaction listing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Taxable Income Adjustments and Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of deductible expenses such as engine depreciation, maintenance, insurance, interest on acquisition debt, losses on disposition of engines, and administrative overhead; add-backs include non-deductible entertainment costs, excessive officers' compensation, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity entries must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if the counterparty is a related party; attach Form 3-25 (International Related-Party Transaction Summary) and demonstrate arm's length rental rates using CUP or TNMM data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Loss Carryforward and Taxable Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Consolidated taxable base determined after applying the statutory loss carryforward period of ten years; the deductible loss carryforward is limited to 60% of the taxable income for large corporations, whereas SMEs may deduct 100%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident shareholder acquired the entity and prior-year losses have been carried forward, be prepared to support the continuity of the same business and beneficial ownership; a change-in-control audit may deny loss carryforward for aircraft-engine leasing assets acquired from a foreign related party.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Tax Calculation, Credits, and Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of national corporate income tax using the progressive 9/19/21/24% rates, addition of the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge, subtraction of investment and R&D tax credits, and netting of interim prepayments made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident equity holders claiming treaty-reduced withholding on cash dividends must attach the final annual corporate tax return as supporting evidence of distributable profits; refunded foreign tax credits are separately claimed under the applicable DTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the final corporate return triggers a non-compliance additional tax of 20% of the unreported corporate income tax; failure to make correct payments by the statutory deadline is subject to an underpayment surcharge of 10% when the return is filed late; daily delayed-payment interest of 0.022% of the unpaid amount is imposed. A fraudulent or wilfully omitted return may expose the corporation to a 40% added penalty and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory rate: 20% dividend income tax on gross payments to a non-resident shareholder plus 10% Local Income Tax surtax on that income tax, producing an aggregate withholding rate of 22%; a treaty can reduce it to between 5% and 15% depending on ownership level and beneficial-ownership requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (1) Determine the non-resident shareholder's jurisdiction of residence and confirm the applicable DTA. (2) Obtain the Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, legalised/apostilled and, if necessary, translated into Korean. (3) Submit the completed Application for Non-Resident Income Tax Exemption/Reduction under a Tax Treaty together with the TRC to the Korean paying corporation before the dividend payment date. (4) The Korean Chusik Hoesa then applies the reduced treaty rates in the withholding return. (5) If the full 22% is initially withheld, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the competent local tax office within three years, attaching all documentation proving beneficial ownership and the availability of DTA relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates for royalties and interest paid to non-residents are 20% plus 10% Local Income Tax surcharge, hence 22% effective; most Korean DTAs reduce royalty withholding to 10–15% and interest withholding to 10%, with a 0–5% rate for bank-qualified interest under certain treaties. All reduced rates are subject to the DTA limitation-on-benefits clause and domestic substance thresholds.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File / Master File attachment is triggered under Article 11 of the International Tax Adjustment Act when annual cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 30,000,000,000; the Master File threshold is additionally triggered when the Korean entity is part of a multinational group whose combined annual group revenue exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000. In practice, a complete transfer-pricing report should be contemporaneous and available even where these thresholds are not breached.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not codify a generic 'Economic Substance Regulations' statute of the UAE/GCC type; however, the National Tax Service applies a force-of-substance doctrine and the International Tax Adjustment Act's anti-treaty-shopping rules. A Korean Chusik Hoesa operating aircraft-engine dry leasing must demonstrate operational substance in Korea, including locally resident directors, management decision-making relating to acquisition and disposition of engines, active negotiation of leases, physical receipt of rent, insurance and maintenance decision authority, and absorption of residual-value risk. A pure nominee or conduit with no functional office, staff, or financial capacity will be recharacterised and denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting aircraft-engine dry-lease income earned by the Korean Chusik Hoesa, disguising lease payments as foreign-currency loans or management fees, failing to declare income held in escrow accounts, or preparing false books showing nominal profitability while funds are diverted to overseas related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, wilful evasion is punishable by imprisonment for up to 10 years or a fine not exceeding 5 times the amount of the evaded tax; the NTS additionally collects the evaded corporate income tax, the underpayment surcharge, and 0.022% daily delinquency interest, and may impose a 40% added tax on fraudulent filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative and responsible directors face personal civil liability for the evaded tax through the corporate veil-piercing doctrine where they authorised false records; practical consequences include travel bans, asset freezing, civil restitution orders, disqualification from directorship, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining the Korean Chusik Hoesa with no full-time staff, no physical operational office, no board meetings in Korea, and no substantive decision-making or risk-bearing capacity, while using the company solely to route aircraft-engine lease income from foreign airlines to a lower-tax jurisdiction through dividends and intra-group payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will deny the applicable DTA benefit under the anti-treaty-shopping provisions of the International Tax Adjustment Act, withhold at the full statutory 22% on dividends, recharacterise the transaction as a Korean-source service or royalty, assess the undeclared corporate income tax, and impose an additional penalty of up to 20% of the underpaid tax; deliberate use of a sham entity may result in criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are merely formal signatories may still have their passports restricted and be held jointly liable for monies diverted if they knew the corporation was a conduit; civil claims by creditors and the State may reach their personal assets where a contumelious disregard of corporate formalities is shown.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing dry-lease rents paid by or to a foreign related enterprise at a rate materially below the arm's length benchmark, failing to maintain contemporaneous comparability studies, or refusing to produce the Local File/Master File upon NTS request during audit of the KRW-scale related-party leasing transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may adjust the Korean entity's taxable income to the arm's length price and correct the related-party transaction amounts; an adjustment produces a penalty of up to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax attributable to the transfer-pricing misstatement, in addition to 0.022% daily late-payment interest; failure to submit documentation itself carries a fixed penalty of up to KRW 500,000,000 for material omission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify or approve falsified intercompany transfer-pricing returns are exposed to personal civil liability for the resulting tax shortfall; aggravated cases involving deliberate documentation destruction or collusion with related parties may result in criminal fines, travel bans, and imprisonment for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign Exchange and AML / Beneficial Ownership Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving aircraft-engine lease rentals via offshore escrow accounts without reporting the receipt under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, structuring multiple Swift wires below reporting thresholds, or concealing the ultimate beneficial owner of the Korean entity when payments are made through jurisdictions with bank secrecy or nominee shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act is punishable by imprisonment for up to three years or a fine not exceeding KRW 100,000,000; the Financial Services Commission may impose administrative fines and the Korea Customs Service may seize undeclared proceeds; the NTS may also impose a 10% aggravated penalty for unlawful receipt of Korean-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute or direct the wire-transfer structure become personally liable for the monetary penalties and may face asset seizure orders and travel restriction notices; a criminal conviction for money laundering or violation of reporting duties can lead to disqualification from directorship and imprisonment, while the corporate veil is pierced where the company was used as a tool for the director's personal financial benefit.
